lens: Does it actually work on an iPad in a truck with gloves and glare, on a phone at a roadside, and on a 13-inch laptop? I judged each proposal against the live measurements (phone 375x812, iPad portrait 768x1024, laptop 1440x900), touch-target and text-size floors, ArcGIS map and 3D SceneView handling, patience on slow connections, one-handed phone use, and whether iPad portrait (768) and iPad landscape (1024) each get a real composition instead of a stretched phone or a squeezed desktop. I judged the proposals as written and did not redesign them.

criteria.name: Implementation cost and fit with the current codebase

perCriterion.reason: One Inbox per role whose rows lead with place and the verb that moves them, plus a Next-step banner on every object page that names the plain status, the owner, what happens after the action and one primary button, answers every first-day failure the walkthroughs recorded (no confirmation on Assign, no location on assessment cards, hidden 'Add reviewer' select, 'Open incident' landing on a table row).

Every one of the 22 screens carries an explicit essential / secondary / hidden split plus a numeric screens-tall budget (Inbox <= 1.5, object page <= 3, form hub <= 2), which is the only way to hold the line after launch.

It is the only proposal with testable field budgets - content within 120px of the top on phone and tablet, one map per phone screen, embedded maps capped at 45vh phone / 50vh tablet with Expand, no nested scroll below 840px, safe-area inset on the bottom bar - and it gives iPad portrait (rail + drill-in) and iPad landscape (rail + 360px list + detail) genuinely different compositions.

perCriterion.criterion: Implementation cost and fit with the current codebase
perCriterion.reason: 64 days is the largest estimate, and Phase 0 redefines Tailwind's default breakpoint names (sm 480 / md 600 / lg 840 / xl 1200) in a repo whose web/src/index.css has no @theme block today, so every unmigrated md:/lg:/xl: class across ~50 screens silently changes meaning mid-migration.

It models all five hand-offs as first-class flows, fixes the branch chief's blocked reviewer task (Add reviewer available in any state), the double submit/review state machines, the office-scoped finalize list and the pre-selected Event Group, all without renaming a field or changing the state machine.

24px floor with 44px on coarse pointers, 12px text floor, no hover-only affordances, list equivalents for every map interaction, aria-current='step' on progress rails, focus-trapped sheets and a contrast check across all three themes are all specified as rules rather than aspirations.

strengths: The only proposal that states measurable field acceptance criteria a QA pass can actually run against the existing baseline: content start <=120px (today 700px on /my-work, /incidents, /assessments at both 375 and 768), 0 tap targets under 44px on coarse pointers (today 120 on /submissions/3), 0 text nodes under 12px (today 74), form hub <=2 screens (today 11.1).

Per-window-class compositions rather than a fluid shrink: bottom bar under 600, 72px icon rail 600-839 with drill-in, 360px list + detail 840-1199, 240px sidebar + 400px list at 1200+. iPad landscape behaves as a small desktop, iPad portrait as a single-pane drill-in - neither is a stretched phone.

Guided flows are route-backed sub-routes (/assessments/:id/delegate), so on a phone they are full pages with a sticky bottom bar and a working browser Back, and on a desktop the same flow renders as a dialog. That is the correct per-class rendering of the same task, and it retires the unlabeled-select dialogs the walkthroughs failed on.

Maps and 3D are treated as a budget, not a feature: one map per phone screen, 45vh/50vh caps with Expand, full-height only on Map and Terrain, SceneView never auto-mounted, WebGL2 + device-memory gate, quality Auto/Low on tablet, 2D fallback, and a 'use an iPad or computer to draw' hint when the phone check fails.

It notices the collision nobody else does: 'Bottom tab bar plus ArcGIS attribution and scale bar can collide on phones; reserve a safe-area bottom inset for map pages.' That is the kind of detail that only shows up when someone has actually looked at a map page on a phone.
Backend asks are enumerated with reasons and none of them renames a field or moves a state; the interim behaviour is documented for the load-bearing one (single review decision).
fatalFlaws: Redefining the default Tailwind breakpoint names in Phase 0 is a build-order hazard on this codebase: with no @theme block in web/src/index.css today, every existing lg:grid-cols-* written for 1024 fires at 840 and every md: written for 768 fires at 600 the moment the token lands, so unmigrated pages reflow on iPad portrait and landscape until each is rewritten. It is mitigable (add new token names alongside sm/md/lg/xl instead of redefining them) but as written it puts the tablet layouts of ~50 screens at risk for the length of a 64-day migration.

Web photo upload for the technical form is scoped as 'backend #7 if needed' in Phase 3 with no stated interim. If it does not land, an engineer on an iPad browser still cannot attach photos - the exact blocker the engineer walkthrough recorded ('There is no way to upload photos, videos or documents from the web submission page') - and the plan does not commit to the honest fallback notice that two of the other proposals write out.
stealThese: The Next-step banner contract on every object page: plain status, who holds it, what happens after the action, one named primary button - and 'Delegated by <name> on <date>' so a role queue reads as a personal hand-off.

The numeric responsive budget as acceptance criteria: content start <=120px, screens-tall caps per page type, one map per phone screen, embedded map 45vh/50vh with Expand, no nested vertical scroll below 840px except inside a map or scene.
Guided flows as route-backed sub-routes that render as pages on phone/iPad portrait and as 640px (hand-off) or 1100px (triage) dialogs on desktop.
'Done recently' and 'Waiting on others' sections in the queue so a triaged report does not vanish from the only page the coordinator knows.
The safe-area reservation for map pages so the bottom tab bar never sits on top of ArcGIS attribution and the scale bar.
Office-scoped finalize list and 'Add reviewer' available in any pre-final state, both of which unblock a role that is blocked today.
evidence: brief-core.md live measurements: /my-work, /incidents, /assessments all start main content at 700px on phone 375x812 and on iPad portrait 768x1024; /submissions/3 is 11.1 screens tall with 120 sub-40px targets and 74 sub-12px text nodes; the proposal's budgets are written directly against these numbers.

web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:164 renders the full navigation as a stacked card at lg:hidden and the sidebar only at lg:block with sticky top-[82px]; workspace mode locks the viewport only at lg (line 138), so phone and iPad-portrait map pages scroll today. The proposal's layout-route + bottom bar / rail / sidebar replaces exactly this.

web/src/index.css contains no @theme block (only :root theme tokens and the .esri-view isolation guard at line 116 plus .map-stack-guard), so the Tailwind breakpoint redefinition in Phase 0 is a new, repo-wide semantic change rather than an edit to existing tokens.

brief-research.md responsive section: Material window size classes at 600/840/1200, canonical list-detail that only splits at expanded width, adaptive navigation (bottom bar under 600, rail above), and the 44x44 coarse-pointer policy - the proposal's breakpoint set and touch rules follow these.

brief-core.md engineer walkthrough: 'There is no way to upload photos, videos or documents from the web submission page' and 'Submission library is display-only' - the basis for the unresolved web-upload flaw.

perCriterion.reason: Making the Incident the only object a person navigates to, with Event Group / Assessment / Submission surviving as tabs and cards inside it, removes the requirement to learn five numbered objects before doing any work, and Home / Incidents / Map are literally the three questions people ask ('what needs me', 'look something up', 'where is it').

The tab split is the minimalism mechanism - each tab has exactly one job with a role-aware essential/secondary/hidden list - and the deliberatelyDropped list retires more duplicated surface (photo-evidence page, submissions worklist, Mission Center, Terrain as a destination) than any other proposal.

Clean per-class compositions with the most disciplined dvh use of the four (map 45 dvh, sheets 90 dvh) and the most honest 3D decision - terrain drawing is simply not offered on compact widths - but it never mentions safe-area insets, and its phone navigation inside the case file is a horizontally scrolling strip of seven tabs.

perCriterion.criterion: Implementation cost and fit with the current codebase
perCriterion.reason: 56 days with a low-risk backend ask (a read-only GET /incidents/{id}/case aggregate plus review/submit consistency) and additive breakpoint tokens that leave legacy sm/md/lg/xl in place, but the case-file route rewrite retires and re-homes the most existing pages at once.

It is the most complete on the domain's loose ends: requested_fields on NEEDS_REPORTER_INFORMATION so the reporter sees which fields to fix, 'Ready to close out' for FINALIZED assessments whose incident is still open, CONSULTED shown as 'For your information' with no decision button, and the Event Group lifecycle ported back from the dead ProjectManagementPanel.

Skip link, focus restore by reusing the existing ModalDialog rather than reimplementing sheets, aria-current='step' on progress rails, 4.5:1 badge contrast with text plus icon, reflow at 320px and a 44px coarse-pointer floor are all stated as rules.

strengths: The only proposal that refuses a task on a device where it is not real: 'Terrain tool: not offered on compact widths; the Site tab shows saved sections as images and a message Draw new cross sections on a tablet or computer.' Placing DEM control points with a finger on a 375px screen is not a task, and saying so is worth more than a heroic phone layout.

Best dvh discipline of the four (11 uses) - map 45 dvh, sheets max 90 dvh, min-h-dvh login wrapper - which is what actually survives the iOS URL bar collapsing and expanding while someone works one-handed.

Hard rule that maps and 3D never sit inside a scrolling container and that no card carries max-h + overflow-auto, which directly kills today's scroll traps (rail 860px, History 420px, Mission Center aside 760px, Event Group history 520px, fixed-height GISA cards).

The strongest returned-work loop in the field: Home quotes the reviewer's comment in full with the flagged section, one tap opens the form with the quote pinned and section J tagged 'Needs attention', and the return has already moved both records back to editable - five taps on an iPad against a blocked ~12-click journey today.
Content capped at 1200px (1440 for tables and maps) so a 27-inch office monitor does not stretch rows, with the cap explicitly relaxed where it would hurt.
The lightest and least speculative backend ask: one read-only aggregate endpoint plus the review/submit consistency fix that every proposal needs anyway.
fatalFlaws: Safe-area insets are absent from the whole document. It specifies a 56px bottom tab bar plus a sticky bottom action bar carrying the page's primary action on phones; on an iPhone with a home indicator, and on an iPad in Split View, that primary button sits in the gesture area unless env(safe-area-inset-bottom) is added. It is a one-line fix but the spec as written puts the single most important control on every detail page in the wrong place on the device the owner cares about.

Seven tabs (Overview, Report, Assessment, Form, Evidence, Site, History) behind a horizontally scrolling 44px strip is the phone navigation for the object that is the whole product. Tabs beyond the third are off-screen with no named affordance for the cut-off, so a first-day engineer looking for 'the form' on a phone or in a 507px iPad Split View column has to discover a horizontal scroll - the same class of failure as today's off-screen Action column on the submissions table.

The two heaviest users of the app - the engineer and the assigned reviewer - reach their real object (the technical form) through an incident wrapper they do not own. That is fine when they arrive by deep link from Home, but any navigation that starts from Incidents costs an extra hop on an iPad in the field, and it makes 'which form' ambiguous the moment an incident carries more than one technical submission, which the assessment panel already supports today.
stealThese: The case file itself: even under a different backbone, the incident record should be one role-aware page whose tabs are the existing backend objects, so nobody has to learn Incident / Event Group / Assessment / Submission before working.
Refuse terrain drawing on compact widths and show saved cross sections as images with 'Draw new cross sections on a tablet or computer'.
dvh everywhere for maps, sheets and full-height workspaces instead of vh, and 'no max-h + overflow-auto cards' as a lint-able rule.

'Ready to close out (N)' on the engineer's home for FINALIZED assessments whose incident is still open - the one place the FINALIZED != RESOLVED policy gap becomes visible to the person who has to act on it.
requested_fields on NEEDS_REPORTER_INFORMATION so the reporter's phone says 'Returned to you: fix Post mile, Route' instead of a generic 'Needs Revision' badge.
GET /incidents/{id}/case as a read-only aggregate so an iPad on LTE makes one request instead of six to eight parallel ones.
The admin 'System health' strip (districts without a coordinator, stuck items, unassigned reviews), which surfaces the silent UNASSIGNED-routing failure mode.
evidence: brief-core.md: /submissions/3 measures 11.1 screens tall on phone with a 532px canvas in a 375px viewport and 180 overflowing elements; iPad portrait shows the location hero alone at 726px - the basis for judging the section-hub replacement and the case-file's under-two-screens claim.

brief-core.md responsive findings on nested scroll: rail max-h-[860px], History max-h-[420px], Mission Center aside max-h-[760px], Event Group history max-h-[520px] - the proposal's no-nested-scroll rule is aimed exactly at these.

brief-research.md map section: 'ArcGIS Scene Viewer requires WebGL2-enabled 64-bit browsers ... Mobile devices must have a minimum of 6 GB RAM' and 'never auto-load 3D on phones' - support for refusing terrain drawing on compact widths.

brief-core.md engineer walkthrough on the revision loop: reviewer notes buried in the fourth card, assessment REVISION_REQUESTED while the submission stays SUBMITTED and locked, 'REJECTED' shown as the badge - the failures the case-file returned-work loop resolves.

brief-research.md responsive section: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 24x24 floor with 44x44 on coarse pointers and the Apple HIG cap of five destinations - the proposal's three-destination set and touch rules follow both.

perCriterion.reason: Plain-language labels, a 'what happens next' sentence from the existing waitingOn() model and one confirm sheet per irreversible action fix real first-day failures, but the information architecture that caused them survives: a coordinator still sees My Work, Incidents, Map, Event Groups and Assessments under More, which is the same four-plausible-homes problem the walkthroughs recorded.

'Each page is cut to the single job it does for the role looking at it' is applied per screen with essential/secondary/hidden lists and the largest plain-status vocabulary of the four, but keeping My Work and Assessments as two pages with the same rail+detail shape means the same records keep appearing twice.

The most codebase-real responsive ladder and the only one that names the two failure modes that actually break an iPad in a truck - map gesture capture and the iOS keyboard colliding with the bottom bar - but its compact/medium boundary at 768 hands landscape phones the tablet composition.

perCriterion.criterion: Implementation cost and fit with the current codebase
perCriterion.reason: 49 days, every route kept (so email links, bookmarks and mobile deep links survive), Tailwind's default breakpoints untouched, existing SidebarNavigation/useNavSections/assessmentModel reused, and every backend item is a sync, a scoping fix or a read-model addition rather than new architecture.

It changes the least and therefore risks the least: same objects, same routes, same permissions model, with the identical set of flagged backend syncs (review/submit consistency, office-scoped finalize, names instead of ids, requested fields for the reporter loop).

A dedicated sweep phase with aria-sort, live regions, focus rings, aria-current, reflow at 320px, three-theme chip contrast and a keyboard path for every map-driven task, on top of primitives that already exist and are unit-tested.

strengths: It is the only proposal that names map gesture capture: 'maps and 3D scenes get a fixed height and require a two-finger or explicit Enable map gestures tap on coarse pointers to avoid scroll traps.' That is the single most common iPad-in-a-vehicle failure - the finger tries to scroll the page and the map eats it - and today the submission page has a SceneView inside a fixed-height card inside a page scroll.

Best offline-ish patience of the four: debounced autosave through the existing Save-draft call, sessionStorage fallback, beforeunload guard, an updated_at precondition on PATCH and a 'Newer changes exist - reload' notice for the case where the same submission was edited offline in the mobile app. That is the realistic model given the mobile app owns true offline work.

Concrete iOS behaviours the others skip: safe-area insets on bottom bars and sheets, and the phone bottom tab bar hiding while an input is focused so the keyboard does not push the primary action off-screen.

Lowest migration risk in this specific repo: it keeps Tailwind's default breakpoint names, keeps all 17 AppShell call sites working while AppShell becomes a layout route, and reuses the tested assessmentModel permissions rather than re-deriving them.
Every legacy route survives as a redirect, which matters in the field because staff arrive from email and mobile deep links, not from the sidebar.

It restates the ArcGIS constraint verbatim ('never set position or z-index on the global .esri-view class; containers size the view'), which is exactly the rule that broke the 3D terrain scenes before.
fatalFlaws: The compact/medium boundary at 768px hands every landscape phone the tablet layout. An iPhone 14 Pro in landscape is 852 CSS px wide and 393 tall, so it gets a 64px icon rail plus a priority-column table with a sticky header in 393px of height - which is the 'squeezed desktop' outcome the owner is complaining about, on the device most likely to be held sideways in a vehicle. Its own research brief sets the boundary at 600 (Material window size classes), and the other three proposals use 600.

It concedes the owner's first goal. A newcomer still has to distinguish My Work from Assessments (identical rail+detail shapes, one to act and one to browse) and still has four record destinations plus Map competing for 'where is the status of an incident'. The proposal fixes the labels, the density and the layout of that confusion but not its cause, and learnability from zero carries the heaviest weight in this evaluation.

It offers 3D cross-section drawing on a phone ('full-height scene; bottom action bar with 44px buttons (scrollable), panels as bottom sheets') behind only a WebGL2 gate. Placing P1..Pn on DEM terrain by finger on a 375px screen is not a task anyone completes in the field, and offering it costs a WebGL2 SceneView load on a phone that may be on LTE.
stealThese: Add new breakpoint tokens alongside sm/md/lg/xl rather than redefining them - this is the migration discipline the winning backbone should adopt regardless of which window-class values it picks.
'Enable map gestures' / two-finger requirement on coarse pointers for any map that sits inside a scrolling page, so the map never steals the page scroll on an iPad.
Hide the phone bottom tab bar while an input is focused, and put env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on every bottom bar and sheet.

Autosave with sessionStorage fallback, beforeunload guard and an updated_at precondition with a 'Newer changes exist - reload' notice, so a web edit cannot silently clobber a mobile offline draft of the same submission.
Keep every legacy route as a redirect so email, bookmark and mobile deep links keep working through the whole migration.
Density modes tied to pointer type (48px coarse / 40px fine / 32px fine-only) persisted per user.
The IntersectionObserver + fixed-anchor warning for scroll-spy jitter on iPad Safari - a real defect the other proposals would hit.
evidence: web/src/index.css has no @theme block, so 'keep Tailwind's defaults' is genuinely free here while redefining them is not; the file also carries the .esri-view isolation-only comment (line 111-116) explaining that forcing position:relative collapses SceneView containers to zero height - the constraint this proposal restates.

web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx: 15 mount sites, aside at lg:hidden (line 164) and the sidebar at lg:block sticky top-[82px] (line 166); workspace mode only locks the viewport at lg (line 138). The layout-route conversion this proposal plans reuses these components rather than replacing them.

brief-research.md: Material window size classes place the compact/medium boundary at 600dp, and Apple HIG warns against switching to the compact layout as soon as an iPad leaves full screen - the basis for judging the 768 boundary a miss for landscape phones and Split View bands.

brief-core.md: the mobile app's offline queue 'replayed in order when online; stops at first failure' and localDrafts.ts as a third kind of 'Draft' - the collision this proposal's updated_at precondition is aimed at.

brief-core.md walkthroughs: 'Four Operations entries (Mission Center, Event Groups, Incidents, Assessments) all plausibly hold the status of an incident' and 'My Work vs Assessments: both pages have an identical rail+detail layout and the same cards, but one is act and one is browse' - the confusion this proposal preserves.

perCriterion.reason: 'The map, the layer chips, the Waiting-on-me count' is a clean anchor for the coordinator and the chiefs, but it asks a newcomer to learn a layer/scope/filter model and a three-detent draggable sheet before doing anything, and a first-day reviewer whose entire job is reading a form and approving it lands on a statewide map that has nothing to do with that job.

Per-screen essential/secondary/hidden lists and a strong rule that anything unlisted goes behind a disclosure, but the hub itself stacks layer chips, a mine chip, scope chips, a status chip, search, a result caption, sort, legend, basemap and refresh time over a map on every device, which is a lot of chrome to carry on a 375px phone.

By far the best map, 3D and orientation thinking of the four - one MapView kept alive in the layout route, selection-driven sheet instead of ArcGIS popups on touch, 1.5x pins with 44px hit areas, clustering only above district scale, viewport never reset, and a genuinely different iPad landscape composition - but iPad portrait is handed the phone composition and the draggable sheet is load-bearing for every task on touch.

perCriterion.criterion: Implementation cost and fit with the current codebase
perCriterion.reason: 61 days, the largest behavioural change (seven pages collapse into one hub with every legacy route redirected), a new always-mounted MapView architecture, and nine backend changes of which the bbox/scope/filter work must land before the hub is honest - Phase 1 ships on client-side filtering over today's 1000-row fetches, which is exactly the payload an iPad on LTE cannot afford.

It fixes the same core defects (single review decision, assignment-scoped reviewer queue, CONSULTED without a decision button, one-commit triage, reviewer management in any state) but turning 'Waiting on me' from a place into a toggleable filter makes it possible for a hand-off to be filtered out of view in a system whose whole job is not losing hand-offs.

'Every map interaction has a list equivalent', keyboard-navigable list with aria-current, inert map at the full detent and a visible 'Expand list' button are all correct, but a nonmodal draggable three-detent sheet is the hardest surface to get right for keyboard and screen-reader users and here it carries reading, deciding and acting on both phone and iPad portrait.

strengths: The best map rulebook of the four and it should be lifted wholesale into whichever direction wins: one MapView mounted in the layout route and kept alive across panel changes, tap-to-select instead of ArcGIS popups (which today are dead copy and get clipped inside a 309px-wide map), pins at 1.5x with 44px hit areas, clustering only above district scale, and the viewport never reset on the 60s poll or on a filter keystroke.

'Exactly one scroll region per screen state: the map is fixed, the sheet/panel scrolls; the SceneView and MapView are never inside a scrolling container' is the single most important touch rule in any of the four documents, and it is stated most crisply here.

The only per-orientation iPad composition: portrait keeps the 72px rail with a bottom sheet, landscape puts a 360px list panel over the map while the map keeps 590px at 1024. That is a real answer to 'does the tablet get its own layout'.

The most honest offline statement: 'Offline use on iPad web is not supported; the mobile app remains the offline tool' with a web autosave-recovery chip only. That respects the constraint instead of implying the browser can do field-offline work.
'Load 3D terrain (about 20 MB)' names the payload before the user commits to it - the right pattern for a truck on LTE, and better than a generic spinner.

Redirecting every legacy route (/my-work, /mission-center, /incidents/:id, /event-groups/:id, /assessments/:id, photo-evidence deep links) keeps field bookmarks and email links alive through the change.
fatalFlaws: The map is the home screen for every role including the assigned reviewer, the approver and the admin. On a phone at a roadside on LTE the first paint of the whole product is basemap tiles, and the queue text lives behind a sheet detent; on an office iPad a reviewer boots an ArcGIS MapView (the proposal itself budgets 1-2s and flags memory on older iPads) to reach a list of two items. This contradicts the guidance the proposal cites: brief-research records Esri's phone-dashboard rule of 'a maximum of one map' with list-first for queues, and lists 'list-first with map as secondary tab' as the correct pattern precisely when the question is 'what needs my action next'.

'Waiting on me is a filter chip with a count, not a page.' In a hand-off machine, a queue that can be switched off, scoped away by a district/office chip or lost when a layer chip changes is a queue that can silently hide work. The count survives on the rail badge, but the items themselves do not have a durable place, and the first-day walkthroughs already show people failing when an item leaves the one page they know.

iPad portrait 768x1024 - the primary field device for engineers and coordinators - gets the phone composition (draggable bottom sheet, two-column rows) rather than a layout of its own. That is the 'stretched phone' outcome the owner is asking to avoid, on the device that matters most.

The nonmodal draggable three-detent sheet is load-bearing for reading records, reviewing status and launching every workflow action on phone and iPad portrait. NN/g (the proposal's own source) says bottom sheets are for short interactions and must never carry approvals; map-first correctly routes the two-step triage to a full-screen route but still fires assessment action sheets from over the list sheet, and the proposal lists sheet correctness for keyboard and screen readers as an open risk.

The engineer's iPad form journey is 29 taps, the highest of the four, because every one of twelve sections costs an open plus a save-and-continue with no way to work down a single scrolling document on a 1024px landscape iPad - which is what the direction-neutral responsive spec actually recommends at that width.
stealThese: The whole map and pin rulebook: one MapView in the layout route kept alive, selection-driven detail instead of ArcGIS popups on touch, docked popups where popups survive, 1.5x pins with 44px hit areas, clustering only above district scale, three map widgets maximum on small maps, and never re-running goTo on a refresh poll or a filter keystroke.
'Exactly one scroll region per screen state; MapView and SceneView are never inside a scrolling container' as a global rule.
'Filter list to map area' as an opt-in spatial filter with a 'Showing 14 of 87 in view' caption and a Clear affordance.
The per-orientation iPad composition: portrait = rail + single pane, landscape = rail + 360px panel over a map that keeps at least 590px.
Naming the 3D payload in the button ('Load 3D terrain (about 20 MB)') and keeping a static preview image until it is pressed.
The honest offline sentence - the mobile app is the offline tool; the web shows an in-session autosave chip only - written into the UI copy so nobody trusts the browser in a canyon.
The route-normalisation alias table so 80, 080, I-80 and R080 all match, which is what blocks the coordinator's map task today.
Auto-collapsing the list rail to a 56px strip below 1366px when a detail panel opens, so a 13-inch laptop never squeezes the panel.
evidence: brief-core.md live measurements of /mission-center: on phone the map begins 912px down and the list at 1502px so they are never visible together; on iPad portrait the map is at 890px and the list at 1644px; only at 1440x900 do map and list sit side by side. This is the real problem map-first is answering, and it is why its map/list rules are the best of the four.

brief-research.md map section: Esri's smartphone dashboard guidance ('a maximum of one map', 'limit the amount of data'), the anti-pattern 'Relying on map popups to reach records on phones', and the pattern 'List-first with map as secondary tab ... when the primary question is what needs my action next' - the guidance the map-as-home decision contradicts on phones and for non-spatial roles.

brief-research.md: 'ArcGIS Scene Viewer requires WebGL2-enabled, 64-bit browsers ... Mobile devices must have a minimum of 6 GB RAM' plus the proposal's own risk entry that MapView init costs 1-2s and memory on older iPads.

brief-core.md Mission Center responsive findings: markers are 11-14px circles and 10-13px diamonds with a single tap that navigates, popups embed a 320px image inside a ~309px map with dockEnabled:false, and back buttons are ~22px tall - the defects map-first's pin and popup rules fix.

spec-responsive.json for the submission detail at lg (field iPad landscape) recommends 'one scrolling document, all sections expanded in a 640-720px column, sticky left section index' - which is why map-first's 29-tap section-by-section iPad journey reads as a phone pattern applied to a tablet.

recommendation:
Build on task-first as the backbone, and merge the case file into it as the incident record. Task-first wins the heaviest criterion outright: a personal Inbox that is a place (not a filter), rows that lead with Route/PM instead of three internal ids, a Next-step banner that says what happens after the button, and hand-offs as short route-backed flows. It is also the only proposal that writes field acceptance criteria you can re-measure against today's baseline - content within 120px of the top (700px today on /my-work, /incidents and /assessments at both 375 and 768), one map per phone screen, embedded maps at 45vh phone / 50vh tablet with Expand, no nested vertical scroll below 840px, zero targets under 44px on coarse pointers (120 today on /submissions/3) and zero text under 12px (74 today).

Merge four things into it.

1. Case-file's object page. Task-first already has an Incident page and an Assessment page; adopt case-file's tab set (Report, Assessment, Form, Evidence, Site, History) so the backend objects become tabs inside the incident rather than separate destinations. That shrinks Records to Incidents + Event Groups, removes the last two of the four plausible homes, and is the piece that makes the system learnable from zero. Take case-file's honest compact refusal for terrain drawing ('draw new cross sections on a tablet or computer', saved sections shown as images), its dvh discipline, 'Ready to close out' for FINALIZED-but-unresolved incidents, requested_fields on the reporter loop, and the GET /incidents/{id}/case aggregate so an iPad on LTE makes one request instead of eight. Cap the phone tab strip at what fits: put the primary action in the sticky bottom bar and move the tail tabs behind a 'More' item rather than relying on horizontal scroll.

2. Map-first's map rulebook, applied to the Map destination and every embedded map but never as the home screen. Lift it verbatim: one MapView mounted in the layout route and kept alive; tap-to-select driving the panel instead of ArcGIS popups on touch; docked popups where popups remain; pins at 1.5x with 44px hit areas; clustering only above district scale; never re-run goTo on a refresh poll or filter keystroke; 'Filter list to map area' with a 'Showing N of M in view' caption; three map widgets maximum on small maps; 'Load 3D terrain (about 20 MB)' with a static preview until pressed; route normalisation so 80 / 080 / I-80 / R080 all match; the list rail auto-collapsing to 56px below 1366px; and above all 'exactly one scroll region per screen state - the map is fixed, the panel scrolls, and MapView/SceneView are never inside a scrolling container'. Also take map-first's per-orientation iPad composition and its honest offline sentence.

3. Progressive's implementation discipline, which is what brings task-first's 64 days down and removes its one build-order hazard. Do not redefine sm/md/lg/xl - add new window-class tokens alongside them and migrate page by page, since web/src/index.css has no @theme block today and ~50 screens still rely on the default meanings. Keep every legacy route as a redirect for email, bookmark and mobile deep links. Take its autosave model (debounced PATCH, sessionStorage fallback, beforeunload guard, updated_at precondition with a 'Newer changes exist - reload' notice against mobile offline drafts), its 'Enable map gestures' / two-finger requirement on coarse pointers, its bottom-bar-hides-on-input-focus behaviour, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on every bottom bar and sheet, its pointer-type density modes, and its IntersectionObserver warning for scroll-spy jitter on iPad Safari.

4. Two non-negotiables from this lens that no proposal fully commits to. First, iPad portrait at 768 must get a stated composition of its own - rail plus single-pane drill-in with the supporting map or photos as a sheet - and it must be re-measured, not inferred; today it is the worst-served width in the app (nav card 577px, then a rail of 860px, then the detail). Second, name the interim for web photo upload in writing: until the attachment endpoint is callable from the browser, every form and evidence surface says 'Photos are added in the ERIS mobile app', because without that an engineer on an iPad browser still cannot finish the form and the first-day journey fails exactly where it fails today.

Map-first should not be the backbone. Its map work is the best in the set and belongs in the final plan, but making a statewide map the first paint for a reviewer on an office iPad, for an admin, and for anyone on a phone at a roadside on LTE inverts the guidance in its own research brief; and turning 'waiting on me' into a chip that can be switched off is the wrong bet for a system whose only real job is not losing a hand-off.
